name: webrain
concept: An autonomous HTTP-layer attacker that walks recon (host disovery via allowlisted CIDR sweep) -> open-port/service enum -> web-app fingerprinting (headers, tech-stack detection, robots/sitemap endpoints) -> multi-vector exploitation (SQLi, stored/reflected XSS, SSRF, path traversal, auth-bypass probes) -> triage by success confidence -> chained escalation to RCE via LFI->log-poisoning, SSRF->internal service attack, or upload->webshell, with per-step state and a final red-team report.
attack_vectors: Reflected & stored XSS with payload delivery
Auth-bypass (JWT alg confusion, default creds, cookie manipulation, parameter tampering)
File upload -> webshell, command-injection and SSTI probes
novelty_angle: Instead of a monolithic scanner, webrain runs exploitation as an iterative planner-evaluator loop that feeds each vector's success/failure signal back into a triage model to re-rank and chain the next best step (e.g. XSS finding unlocks an SSRF pivot), rather than hammering vectors blindly in fixed sequence.
scope_gate: Reads only a user-supplied allowlist: loopback, RFC1918 private ranges, and an explicit lab CIDR flag; every target IP/host/redirect and every chained pivot URL is re-validated against the allowlist before each request; any out-of-scope target aborts the run; WARN banner printed on first launch.
